calls.head: Don’t buy Kuemper’s slump against the Senators
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Kuemper has been shaky against the Senators, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.
calls.call: If Kuemper starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .904 than to his .837 against the Senators.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Senators pour it on late
paras: Mats Zuccarello struck first for the Kings early in the first. The Kings’ Erik Gustafsson left late in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was ruled out for 2-4 weeks with an upper-body injury. Nick Cousins tied it up for Ottawa with just under a minute left in the period. The third period was a wild one. Tim Stützle put the Senators ahead for good just 30 seconds into the period. Stephen Halliday made it 3-1 on the power play early in the period, and that insurance goal turned out to be the winner. Stützle struck again less than two minutes later to make it 4-1, but Quinton Byfield cut Ottawa’s lead to 4-2 just under three minutes later. He added an assist for a three-point night.

The Senators had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Kings 28-21. Linus Ullmark made 19 saves for the Sens, and Anton Forsberg stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. Ullmark has won five straight starts. By our Swing measure, Tyler Kleven had the best night of anyone, even without a point.
The Senators killed all four Kings power plays. The Senators improved to 15-6-3 and climbed into first in the Atlantic, while the Kings fell to 7-12-2, seventh in the Pacific.
